<reason>A established licensing’s incremental benefit: independent acceptance of safeguards before potentially irreversible diffusion, rather than testing obligations alone. It answered pressure on upgrades and expertise with targeted reassessment, continued access to authorized versions, and a clear distinction between technical knowledge and public decision authority. B raised substantial delay and competition costs, and A did not fully establish that administrative safeguards would contain them. However, B repeatedly overstated foreign circumvention as eliminating licensing’s benefits and treated authorization as mere paperwork. A’s narrower comparison—bounded review costs against reducing inadequately assessed EU exposure—survived more convincingly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A challenged why foreign availability supposedly defeats licensing but not B’s withdrawal orders. B distinguished their timing and targeting, but did not establish why licensing could not reduce ordinary EU exposure without eliminating global access. This materially weakened B’s claim that the gate imposes costs without providing protection.</best_rebuttal>
